name: Magori
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Dutton, Tom E. 1976. Magori and similar languages of south-east Papua (Pacific Linguistics; not located online)

sources.citation: OLAC listing for Magori [zgr] (language-archives.org, Wayback id_ capture Nov 2025).
sources.note: Lists PARADISEC TD1-P00580 (Dutton 1980 Magori text/vocab/sentences audio), TD1-P120/121/122 (1972 Magori survey audio), SIL archive 58555 'Magori Wordlist 1973' (not online), Rosetta Swadesh list; no grammar/phonology description.

sources.citation: Rosetta Project. n.d. Magori Swadesh List (archive.org rosettaproject_zgr_swadesh-1, uploaded 2010).
sources.note: ~45 glosses in plain orthography, no stress marks, no source named.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. PL C-98. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6201.R67 1988 (also: archive.org controlled lending)
sources.note: Magori pp.192-195, 205 and Table 30 (Central Papuan consonant correspondences): diachronic only; no Magori prosody. Bibliography lists Dutton 1980a 'A Magori vocabulary' and 1980b 'Magori grammar notes', TS, ANU.

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom. 1982. Borrowing in Austronesian and non-Austronesian languages of coastal south-east mainland Papua New Guinea. In Halim, Carrington & Wurm (eds), Papers from 3ICAL vol. 1: Currents in Oceanic, 109-177. PL C-74.
sources.note: Appendix 3 'Ouma and Magori sound systems' p.166: phoneme inventory and allophones; glottal stop suspect; 'There are no consonant clusters in Ouma or Magori, and all syllables are open.' Sec. 3.1 p.114: Magi bilingualism 'interfering with the phonology'. No statement on stress.

sources.citation: Dutton, T.E. 1976. Austronesian languages: eastern part of south-eastern mainland Papua. In Wurm (ed.), PL C-39: 321-333 (Magori entry p.302/327 region of vol. 2).
sources.note: Survey entry: ~160 speakers, two villages; 'A grammatical sketch and vocabulary appear in Dutton 1971' (the LSPNG mimeo). Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Dutton, T.E. 1976. Magori and similar languages of South-East Papua. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 581-636. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 4.5.2.6.1 'Phonological evidence' p.594: five vowels, simple consonant system (p t k glottal b d g m n v r), allophony, 'All syllables are open and there are no consonant clusters.' Table 2 comparative vocabulary (pp.610ff) printed without stress marks. Nothing on stress/accent anywhere in the chapter.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew. 1975. The relationships of the Austronesian languages of Central Papua: a preliminary study. In T.E. Dutton (ed.), Studies in languages of central and south-east Papua, 3-105. PL C-29.
sources.note: Sec. 3.10 pp.15-16 Magori (data from Dutton's 1971b sketch); sec. 4 is historical phonology (POC reflexes) only. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Dutton, T.E. 1971. Languages of South-East Papua: a preliminary report. In Dutton, Voorhoeve & Wurm, Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14, 1-46. PL A-28.
sources.note: Sec. 3.0 p.9: Magori location, villages (Magori 124, Deba 39, ?Laua 31), Mailu influence. No phonology; silent on stress.
Nothing; classification and contact history only.

sources.citation: Dutton, T.E. 1980b. Magori grammar notes. Typescript, Department of Linguistics, RSPacS, Australian National University (cited in Ross 1988 PL C-98 bibliography); with Dutton 1980a 'A Magori vocabulary', TS.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only grammar-length treatment of Magori by its sole fieldworker; if any stress statement or stress-marked vocabulary exists it is here. Possibly among Dutton's papers at ANU/PARADISEC.

sources.citation: Dutton, T.E. 1971b. Magori: its nature and relationship to other languages of South-East Papua. Paper presented to the Linguistic Society of Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby, August 1971. Mimeographed.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Contains the 'short grammatical sketch and vocabulary' that Dutton 1976 and Pawley 1975 draw on; may include phonological notes beyond the published summary.
